title: POC Weekly Sync - App Integration / SDK + Tool/Function Calls / Structured Output
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on application integration. Reviewed SDK function-calling implementation, structured-output schema validation, flaky tool-call retries, and next steps for running end-to-end tests and security checklist. Agreed to run 10k sample requests and share metrics next week.
topics: structured JSON output and schema validation
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-16 15:00 PST, Duration 46m. Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Arun (Redwood SE), Jared (Neptune Lead Eng), Priya (PM), Carlos (Infosec), Aisha (SWE)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, hope the time's still good. quick agenda: sdk integration, function calls, structured output issues you ran into, and security questions.
[00:18] Jared: Yep all good. Thanks Samir. We shipped the SDK yesterday and ran initial tests, Lina did a lot of the pairing.
[00:26] Lina: Yeah I paired with Aisha on auth and the basic generate + tool call flow. main thing we saw was a few malformed structured outputs coming back when the sequence had tool calls in the middle. e.g. we expect top-level "invoice" object but sometimes we get invoice as string or missing fields.
[00:43] Aisha: to add, our app pipeline validates schema with the JSON schema we provided. about 3% of the responses failed validation on a 1k run, mostly around date formats and nested arrays.
[00:55] Arun: that's consistent with tokenization boundaries and occasionally the model truncates or returns escaped chars. we pushed a config that enforces stricter response_format with required fields and an alternate parser in the SDK.
[01:12] Priya: can you explain the SDK parser change? we noticed sdk.json_to_struct(...) in the sample was swallowing errors.
[01:22] Lina: yeah so the current SDK provides two helpers: parse_structured_output and validate_schema. parse_structured_output will attempt a best-effort repair of common issues - unescaped quotes, trailing commas, common lemmata - but we added a strict flag that returns raw output + error when set. that let Aisha's pipeline fail fast and route failures to a secondary tool-call repair flow.
[01:46] Carlos: from security standpoint we need to ensure any repair logic doesn't send PII to external repair services, is that possible?
[01:54] Samir: yes, repair runs are fully local by default in the SDK; if you opt into sending to the hosted repair endpoint you have to enable it and the data will be encrypted with your customer key. we also log repair attempts to audit logs if you enable that submodule.
[02:14] Carlos: ok we want audit logs and KMS-backed encryption for any hosted processing. can you share SOC2 artifacts and the KMS integration guide?
[02:22] Samir: we'll share the security pack and integration docs after the call.
[02:28] Jared: back to function/tool calling: we implemented two tool integrations so far: an invoice lookup microservice and a currency-conversion tool. the problem surfaces when tool-call returns slow or errors; the LLM sometimes emits the wrong function signature which breaks the SDK's dispatch.
[02:46] Lina: right, we saw cases where the model returns a function name that's slightly mis-spelled, e.g. "get_invoice_by_id" vs "getInvoiceById" and that causes the runtime to not match. SDK has fuzzy matching heuristics now, and you can supply explicit tool aliases in the request.
[03:06] Aisha: were those heuristics on by default? we want deterministic behavior for production.
[03:11] Arun: heuristics are off by default for Dedicated/private installs; on hosted they're enabled but you can set match_mode: exact|alias|fuzzy in the call options.
[03:23] Priya: nice. also we ran into retry/backoff behavior - the SDK retried on 500s but sometimes it replays tool calls that are non-idempotent (charge payments). how do we prevent that?
[03:36] Lina: great callout. SDK supports idempotency tokens for tool calls. you mark the tool as idempotent=false in the tool registration manifest and the SDK will not automatically retry; instead it surfaces the error to your app, or you can provide a custom retry handler. there's also a dry_run flag for previewing tool-call arguments without executing side effects.
[03:56] Carlos: for compliance we need logs of tool-call arguments but redaction of sensitive fields. can the SDK redact on export?
[04:05] Samir: yes, the SDK includes a redact_schema option where you provide keys to mask before logs are sent to audit. you can also route logs to your own SIEM via the log forwarder hook.
[04:18] Jared: another observation: structured output sometimes has numeric fields as strings so downstream type checks fail. is there a canonical converter?
[04:27] Lina: there's a typed_transform helper that coerces fields per the JSON Schema you give it. it tries safe conversions ("42" -> 42) and will error on ambiguous conversions unless you pass allow_coerce=true.
[04:40] Aisha: we used allow_coerce for the POC and saw fewer issues but worried about silent data corruption.
[04:47] Arun: recommend running strict validation in CI and allow_coerce only at the boundaries where you control the inputs, we can provide a validation harness you can run locally.
[04:58] Priya: let's talk about tests and benchmarks - Jared you mentioned a 10k request run?
[05:05] Jared: yes we're planning to run 10k user-simulated requests through the app-level integration to measure error rates, latency and cost per 1k tokens. currently our local run showed average latency 420ms on hosted sandbox, cost estimates look fine but we need to run realistic sequences with tool calls and long context windows.
[05:26] Lina: if you want we can provide a benchmark harness that replays requests with preserved timing and KV cache warmups. that will give you predictable numbers and help validate batching settings.
[05:36] Jared: please. also we need to validate cold-start behavior and KV cache hits during peak.
[05:42] Samir: we'll include a script that simulates batch sizes and sequence length distribution; for Dedicated we can show projected throughput numbers.
[05:50] Carlos: security: one more ask - can we surface per-tool ACLs in the console and via SDK so only certain service accounts can call payment-related tools?
[05:59] Arun: yes per-tool RBAC is supported in the control plane; SDK will enforce the token scopes and return explicit permission errors if token lacks tool:invoke. we'll document the IAM mapping.
[06:13] Priya: any notes on model pinning and fallback? sometimes we want a cheaper quantized variant for lower-priority traffic.
[06:21] Lina: yes the SDK/Runtime support model_variant preference in the call options. you can pass variant: ["redwood-lite-q4","redwood-1-std"] and the router will pick the top available, fallbacking gracefully. also automatic fallback preserves structured output schema but may degrade quality; we'll include a regression test for that.
[06:43] Aisha: small question about streaming - does streaming with function/tool calls send partial tool args? we saw truncated json in a partial stream and our parser choked.
[06:53] Arun: streaming returns events: text_chunk, function_call_start, function_call_chunk, function_call_end. the SDK buffers until function_call_end before attempting to parse. the partial chunks shouldn't be passed to the parser. if you saw truncation that means the server closed the connection prematurely; we'll investigate.
[07:13] Jared: ok. we're also trying to wire telemetry: per-route latency, per-tool failure rate and structured-output validation rate. can we emit those metrics to a Prometheus endpoint?
[07:23] Lina: yes the runtime exposes a metrics endpoint and the SDK can emit client-side metrics; we'll share the prometheus scrape config.
[07:30] Priya: timeline: we want to move from POC to pilot in 3 weeks if the 10k run is under 5% validation failures and security checks pass.
[07:40] Samir: that sounds reasonable. we'll help with benchmarks and security docs.
[07:45] Carlos: one more security nit - data retention in logs. we need to set retention to 90 days and ensure the hosted audit logs can be purged on request.
[07:55] Samir: retention policy configurable per account; hosted audit logs support deletions and export. we'll include that in the security pack.
[08:03] Aisha: actionable bug: during the last run, the SDK raised a parse exception but swallowed the original model output in the error message, making debugging hard. can SDK include raw_output in the error payload?
[08:15] Lina: yes we can add raw_output to debug mode only; for security we won't include raw_output in standard logs unless debug is explicitly enabled.
[08:25] Jared: great. any expected impact on size of logs with raw_output?
[08:29] Samir: only in debug enabled runs; we recommend using it short-term for triage.
[08:35] Priya: ok let's recap next steps.
[08:38] Samir: quick recap: Redwood to provide benchmark harness and scrape config; security pack + KMS integration guide + SOC2 artifacts; SDK patch to include raw_output in debug; a small patch to make tool aliasing explicit in sample manifest; we'll run a 10k replay and deliver metrics next week.
[08:58] Jared: and Neptune to run 10k job, share failure logs, run CI with strict validation, and confirm timeline for pilot.
[09:06] Carlos: Neptune to confirm retention and RBAC requirements in writing.
[09:12] Samir: good. we'll follow up with calendar invite for a mid-week sync and share a checklist. thanks everyone.
[09:18] meeting end
